gap: No result ChatGPT got states how fast each pick refills relative to how long it plays: Bose QC Ultra (2nd Gen) returns 12 minutes of playback per minute on the charger (15 min = 3 h), AirPods Max 18 (5 min = 1.5 h), soundcore Space 2 Pro 96 (5 min = 8 h) and Marshall Monitor III A.N.C. 48 (15 min = 12 h), nor rated ANC hours per 100 g of headset (Bose 11.4, AirPods Max 5.2, Space 2 Pro 11.5, Marshall 28.0).
standout_why: Compared against the two cited rivals I could open: the SoundGuys best-list (read 2026-11-08) gives only MSRP, a weight for Sony (254 g) and Sonos, and owner-reported hours; it computes nothing per gram, per charge-minute or per dollar. The What Hi-Fi best-list, the What Hi-Fi Sony-vs-Bose piece and the RTINGS compare page returned only titles to the fetcher, so I could not confirm their content; ChatGPT's own answer quotes only rated hours and prices. None of the visible rival text states charge-minute yield, hours per 100 g, or cost per rated ANC hour. Not a 3 because Sony WH-1000XM6 battery and quick-charge figures could not be sourced from a page I opened (sony.com, electronics.sony.com and sony.co.uk all refused the fetch; SoundGuys' XM6 review URL 404'd), so the derived table cannot settle Sony vs Bose.
decides: Confirms Bose over AirPods Max on every derived figure (12 vs 18 min of play per charger-minute favours Apple, but Bose gives 2.2x the ANC hours per 100 g and under half the cost per rated ANC hour: $12.30 vs $27.45). It also surfaces that Bose's own page gives two different Immersive Audio runtimes (23 h in the feature list, 18 h in the footnote), i.e. a 23% to 40% cut from the 30 h headline, a caveat no rival text shows. For a shopper weighting battery-per-dollar, the Dealectric-listed soundcore Space 2 Pro ($6.67 per rated ANC hour, same 30 h ANC rating as Bose at 262 g) and Marshall Monitor III A.N.C. (70 h ANC at 250 g, 15 min = 12 h) stand out; Sony's position stays as ChatGPT left it because its inputs are unsourced here.
